subject: NeptuneHealth: BYOK & on-prem KMS architecture review
messages:
From: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@neptunehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@neptunehealth.com
Date: 2025-08-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial: BYOK for private deployment at NeptuneHealth

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this on. NeptuneHealth is heading toward a private deployment in our primary VPC + co-lo for PHI workflows. Before procurement we'll need a short architecture review specific to BYOK/HSM integration, rotation procedures, and operator separation controls so our InfoSec and procurement teams can sign off.

Attached is our standard BYOK questionnaire (neptune_byo_questionnaire_v2.pdf). High-level asks:
- Where/how private keys are stored and who can unseal during emergency
- Rotation window and how to avoid downtime for live inference workloads
- Network egress and cross-connect constraints (we're a no-public-egress environment)
- Audit trail: what events you log (unseal, key-create, wrap/unwrap, operator access)

Can you provide a one-page architecture diagram + a short runbook and proposed test/cutover window? We're hoping to finalize vendor decisions the week of Sep 8.

Appreciate it —
Alice
Security Architect, NeptuneHealth

Attachment: neptune_byo_questionnaire_v2.pdf (pdf, 240KB)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@neptunehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-08-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial: BYOK for private deployment at NeptuneHealth

Alice —

Thanks for the questionnaire. We've reviewed it and sketched an internal proposal (attached). High-level summary up front:

- Key custody: Customer-held master key (BYOK) protected in your HSM. Redwood will provision an ephemeral wrapping key per deployment; we will never persist your master unwrapped key. For emergency unseal we support split-operator unseal with threshold N-of-M KMS operator tokens.

- Rotation: Support two rotation modes: live key-rotation (re-wrap approach) for minimal latency impact, and scheduled rolling-rekey (blue/green) for full-surface rotations. For live inference workloads we recommend the re-wrap approach (no restart) with a short token flush (~<200ms on average); we outline fallback to canary node drains if needed.

- Network: Because you require no public egress, we propose a cross-connect into your private VLAN with a dedicated subnet for the key-service cluster and a bastion jump-host for operator access. Mutual TLS + client certs enforced for all KMS control-plane traffic; data-plane model traffic remains separate.

- Auditing: We log key lifecycle events (create/rotate/destroy/wrap/unwrap/unseal), operator sessions (start/stop/commands), and administrative ACL changes. Logs are signed and forwarded to your SIEM over the cross-connect; we also support sealed log replication into an HSM-wrapped archive.

I've attached: redwood-onprem-kms-proposal-v1.docx and a quick network sketch (network-segmentation-draft.png).

Next steps I'd propose: 1) Technical deep-dive with your infra/security + our ops (60 min), 2) Ops cutover plan and test window (we suggest Sep 3–5 or Sep 10–12), 3) Pre-cutover dry-run in staging with telemetry validation.

Marissa and Kimberly — please review the proposal and add any operational constraints or known latency impacts.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Partnerships & Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-onprem-kms-proposal-v1.docx, network-segmentation-draft.png

Subject: Re: Initial: BYOK for private deployment at NeptuneHealth

Adding operational details from runtime side — quick notes for the devops/security reviewers: 

- Live re-wrap rotation: we rotate the wrapping key and issue a new wrapped copy of the model-serving token. For typical seq-latency profiles we observe 120–250ms median added per token fetch during the ephemeral KV refresh when a node pulls a freshly wrapped token. That cost is amortized if prefix caching is enabled.

- KV cache considerations: during large rotations we'll shard rotations to groups of hosts to avoid global cache invalidation. We provide a config knob to control max parallel host re-wraps.

- Emergency unseal: our recommended pattern is 3-of-5 operator split (threshold 3) with each operator using a hardware-backed credential (YubiKey / HSM-backed client cert). We keep operator interactions auditable and require multi-party authorizations for any master key unwrap.

- DR and key escrow: Neptune asked about escrow — we can support a sealed-offsite escrow where an encrypted backup of wrapped master keys is stored in your vault. Escrow retrieval requires both operator threshold and a Neptune-side administrative token.

- TLS + MTLS: all control-plane endpoints require mutual TLS + signed CN matching operator identity; we also support additional network ACLs at the subnet and port level.

I'll prepare a short runbook excerpt (15–20 steps) for the dry-run.

—Marissa
Senior Applied Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Initial: BYOK for private deployment at NeptuneHealth

Operational checklist + proposed test windows (short):

1) Prep (Week -2): Exchange certs, establish cross-connect ACLs, provision staging HSMs with Neptune's BYOK public key, and deploy a staging key-service cluster.
2) Dry-run (Week -1): Execute operator unseal drill and one live re-wrap rotation on staging, validate logs shipped to Neptune SIEM, run latency smoke tests. 
3) Cutover (Preferred Sep 10-11):
   - 00:00–04:00 UTC: Canary cluster cutover (1/8 hosts) — validate metrics and audit logs.
   - 04:00–10:00 UTC: Incremental host group re-wraps in parallel groups (max parallelism configurable).
   - Contingency: automatic rollback to previous wrapping key within 30 minutes; manual operator rollback requires 2-of-3 signature.
4) Post-cutover (Day +1): Full audit review, export signed event log to Neptune secure bucket.

Notes: We recommend keeping maintenance windows during off-peak PHI ingestion hours. For ultra-low-latency inference lanes, enable per-route caching and reduce re-wrap parallelism.

Please confirm which window you prefer. Also flag any procurement constraints (e.g., HSM model list, FIPS/CC requirements).

—Kimberly
Principal DevOps Engineer
Redwood Inference

Vanessa / team —

This is excellent and addresses the majority of our concerns. A few follow-ups before we lock the Sep 10-11 window: 
- HSM models: please enumerate supported vendor models and proof of FIPS/CC where applicable.
- Escrow retrieval SLA: clarify the manual steps and expected turnaround for emergency retrieval (we require under 4 hours for key recovery in P1 incidents).
- Can you provide the short runbook excerpt Marissa mentioned as a PDF we can attach to our procurement docs?

If you can send those three items by end of week we'll route to procurement and legal for the final SOW. Prefer Sep 10-11; we'll confirm once we validate the HSM model list.

Thanks,
Alice
Security Architect, NeptuneHealth
